contexts.text: The voice of the roaring of a lion () = falsity.
To roar = from power to speak and act against the Hells, which want to carry man off... Illustrated.
To cry as a lion roareth () = a grievous lamentation concerning the Church, and that it has been taken away from Him. Explained, Illustrated. AE 601.
That a roaring = grievous lamentation. Illustrated.
Jehovah is here compared to a roaring lion () because... to roar = the ardour of defending against evils and falsities. Illustrated. AE 601:5.
To roar = desire.
The roaring of a lion () = the desire to destroy and make desolate.
To roar = the effect of grief, on account of the desolation of Divine truth in the Church. Illustrated.

To roar, or the roaring of a lion, = ardent affection to defend Heaven and the Church, and thus to save the Angels of Heaven and the men of the Church, which is effected by destroying the falsities of evil by the Divine truth and its power. AE 601:11, Illustrated. AE 850:15.

In the opposite sense, to roar, and the roaring of a lion, = a burning cupidity to destroy and devastate the Church, which is effected by destroying Divine truth by the falsities of evil. These things are signified by the roaring of a lion, because a lion roars when it is hungry and seeks its prey, and also when it is enraged against its enemies. AE 601:11, Illustrated.
The defence of the faithful by the Lord by means of Divine truth, is described by Jehovah shall roar out of Zion ().
He shall roar like a lion, because He shall roar () = their defence by means of Divine truth.
The lion hath roared, who will not fear? () = a powerful revelation and manifestation of Divine truth.
The voice of the roaring of the young lions () = grief on account of the desolation of Divine truth.
Their burning desire to destroy Divine truth by means of the falsities of evil, is signified by, They shall roar together like lions, they shall give forth a roaring like lions' whelps ().
The young lions roar against him, they give forth their voice () = the desolation of Divine truth in the Church by the falsities of evil.
The voice of his roaring () = the destroying falsity of evil.

Jehovah shall roar from on high, and utter His voice from the habitation of His holiness () = testification of grief in Heaven on account of the vastation of Divine truth. In roaring He shall roar against their dwellings = grievous grief and lamentation over all things of the Church.
Jehovah shall roar from Zion () = grievous grief.
(Jehovah's) roaring is like that of a lion, He roareth as the young lions () = grief and lamentation over the vastation of Divine truth in the Church through the falsities of evil.
That roaring = grievous lamentation from grief of heart. Illustrated.
Enemies have roared in the midst of thy feast () = that falsities have destroyed all things of worship.
